children: Two measures of inflation that are critical to getting the topline figure back toward 2% moved the wrong direction in October, Glenmede's Jason Pride says in a note. The first is services less rent of shelter, which rose 0.5%, its firmest reading since May, Pride says. That extends the sticky services dynamic that has been a major obstacle to restraining price growth, he says. The measure needs to average out near 0.2% before it looks like inflation is heading back in the right direction, Pride says. The second is commodities less food, energy and used cars, which rose 0.4% in October, its firmest since January, he says. That strips out the most volatile components within goods, Pride says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)
